items.statement: Peningkatan Kinerja ELC PLTMH Berbasis QLSTM
QLSTM is a temporal model and supervisory gain scheduler, not a direct controller and not a metaheuristic gain optimizer.
Ask to what extent QLSTM adaptive PI improves frequency response compared with fixed PI and LSTM adaptive PI.
Compare fixed PI, LSTM-PI and QLSTM-PI using technical indicators and paired statistical testing.
Train, validation and test data are split by separate scenarios.
Planned disturbances include step, multi-step and random load variations.
Evaluation includes peak deviation, settling time, IAE, ITAE, gain estimation quality and computational burden.
Estimated gain is bounded and exponentially smoothed before application.
Formal statistical hypotheses compare QLSTM-PI against fixed PI and LSTM-PI.
Initial 70:15:15 split is applied to scenario counts.
Paired t-test or Wilcoxon, significance threshold, 95% CI, effect size and multiple comparison correction are planned.
Sensitivity analysis planned for window length, update interval, smoothing factor, qubits and VQC depth.
Expected empirical evidence of added value of QLSTM over classical LSTM.
Gain limits are described as a safe or stable gain range.
QLSTM uses quantum simulation in a hybrid quantum-classical framework, not quantum hardware.
Three configurations are compared: fixed PI, LSTM-PI and QLSTM-PI.
